why: All three checks pass. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 168 under '### Authentication precedence' ('When multiple credentials are present, Claude Code chooses one in this order:'). The whole line is that one sentence plus the 'See third-party integrations' pointer — no reversing second half. The only qualifier on the page is line 175, which says a signed-in Claude apps gateway session outranks the cloud-provider tier; we ship no Claude apps gateway session, so it does not soften the claim for us. (2) CITED LINES CORRECT: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245 builds the subprocess env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}`, and :260-262 deletes exactly CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL under the comment 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path.' `grep -rna` (NUL-safe) over the whole tree finds CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY in no source file at all, and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX only in config/managed-env.ts:126 — a different subsystem (the server-managed-settings withheld-env classifier for a cached policy `env` block), not the SDK subprocess env, so it does not strip anything here. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, THREE LAYERS: (a) one layer up, apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28-77 spawns the user's login shell (`$SHELL -l -i -c env`) in the packaged macOS app and copies EVERY variable into process.env, filtering only keys starting with `VITE_` — so an ambient CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX/FOUNDRY in .zshrc really does reach process.env before any agent is created; (b) the second strip list has the same hole — claude-agent.ts:911-917 does the 'clean state' delete of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars() (llm-connections.ts:931-935, the same three Bedrock keys), and omits Vertex/Foundry too, so nothing upstream already handled it; (c) one layer down, a positive control on the binary we actually ship: `strings -a node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` (SDK 0.3.183) hits CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX 20x and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY 17x, and sdk.mjs contains the literal branch `Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE)` — the runtime we spawn does read them. NOT a recorded owner decision: the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches an env strip list. NOT a deliberate product difference either: dropping the Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows and shipping no Vertex/Foundry provider is exactly why an ambient Vertex/Foundry toggle is unwanted, and the repo already asserts the invariant for Bedrock — it is applied inconsistently, not waived.
correctedState: Confirmed with three corrections of scope. (i) The hole exists in TWO strip lists, not one: options.ts:260-262 (subprocess env) and llm-connections.ts:931-935 CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS, cleared from process.env by claude-agent.ts:917 in ClaudeAgent.postInit. A fix must widen both. (ii) The gap is wider than the doc's three names: the shipped SDK 0.3.183 branches on five cloud-provider toggles — BEDROCK, VERTEX, FOUNDRY, ANTHROPIC_AWS and MANTLE. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS is undocumented on this page and absent from our source too; CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE is finding f116, the same root cause at the same two sites, so f116 and f118 are one edit. Additionally ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN — precedence tier 2, ABOVE the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that postInit does set — appears nowhere in the Claude subprocess path (only in managed-env.ts:141), so an ambient bearer token in the user's shell outranks the connection's key by the same mechanism. (iii) Reachability: the Claude SDK subprocess only spawns in a build with NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE enabled (default off; factory.ts:182, :430, :470, :580, :748, :897 throw/return 'Claude support is not included in this build.'), so the hazard is confined to Claude-enabled builds — real, since that flag is what the Bedrock strip already exists to protect. 'Silently' is accurate only when the ambient shell carries a complete Vertex/Foundry configuration (project id, region, credentials); a half-configured shell produces a routing error instead of a silent provider swap.
